result:
I found real disorder and submitted a model that describes it. R1 dropped from 0.0491 to 0.0380 and wR2 from 0.161 to 0.139.

All three carboxyphenyl-thiolate ligand rings (on C15, C26 and C37) are disordered over two ring orientations that pivot about the ipso–para axis, at roughly 50:50, 55:45 and 53:47. In the original model their atoms had Ueq of 0.2–0.65 Å², the rings had impossible geometry (for example C47 sat 2.25 Å from C42, which I had to move), and the difference map had 2–2.7 e/Å³ peaks at exactly the alternative ring and carboxyl-O positions. I rebuilt each ring as idealised PART 1 / PART 2 positions with riding H atoms. Each ring's carboxyl O/OH atoms are split with the same free variable as the ring, restrained with SADI, FLAT, DFIX and DANG.

Ag5 and Ag6 also have weak minor sites about 0.92 Å away, which removed the two largest peaks (2.9 and 2.7 e/Å³). These refine to only 9% and 4%, so the Ag6 split in particular is marginal.

After the changes every carbon has Ueq of 0.04–0.15 Å². The largest leftover peaks (under 1.9 e/Å³) sit near the O atoms of the two untouched benzoate carboxyls (on C7 and C14). I judged those too weak to justify adding more disorder.
